metadata.title: Mechanism-first rare disease knowledge graph
metadata.demo_persona: A patient advocacy leader for STXBP1-related disorder
metadata.scope: Small hackathon MVP dataset focused on STXBP1-related disorder, Dravet syndrome, and CDKL5 deficiency disorder.
metadata.disclaimer: Prototype dataset for demo and product validation only. It is not medical advice and should be reviewed by qualified clinicians and researchers before use.

nodes.label: STXBP1-related disorder
nodes.details: A rare developmental and epileptic encephalopathy caused by pathogenic variants in STXBP1. Key challenges include early-onset seizures, developmental delay, intellectual disability, movement differences, and limited disease-specific treatments.
nodes.plain_language: Children and adults whose brain cells have trouble communicating because one STXBP1 copy is not working as expected.

nodes.label: Dravet syndrome
nodes.details: A severe childhood-onset developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, most often caused by loss-of-function variants in SCN1A. It has comparatively mature clinical trial experience for seizure outcomes.
nodes.plain_language: A related epilepsy community with trial experience that other communities can learn from.

nodes.label: CDKL5 deficiency disorder
nodes.details: A developmental epileptic encephalopathy caused by pathogenic variants in CDKL5, with early-onset seizures, severe developmental impairment, and synaptic development abnormalities.
nodes.plain_language: A peer rare-disease community facing similar early-life seizure and development challenges.

nodes.label: STXBP1
nodes.details: Encodes syntaxin-binding protein 1 / MUNC18-1, a presynaptic protein required for synaptic vesicle docking and neurotransmitter release.
nodes.plain_language: The gene that helps nerve cells release messages to each other.

nodes.label: SCN1A
nodes.details: Encodes the Nav1.1 voltage-gated sodium channel. Loss of function is strongly associated with Dravet syndrome and impaired inhibitory interneuron firing.
nodes.plain_language: A gene for a sodium channel that helps neurons fire correctly.

nodes.label: CDKL5
nodes.details: Encodes cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5, a kinase important for brain development, dendritic growth, synapse formation, and neuronal function.
nodes.plain_language: A gene important for how young brain cells grow and build connections.

nodes.label: Presynaptic vesicle release / SNARE regulation
nodes.details: A mechanism involving docking, priming, and fusion of synaptic vesicles so neurons can release neurotransmitters.
nodes.plain_language: The message-release machinery at the end of a neuron.

nodes.label: Excitation-inhibition imbalance
nodes.details: A shared epilepsy mechanism where the balance between excitatory and inhibitory signaling is disrupted, making seizure networks easier to trigger.
nodes.plain_language: The brain's accelerator and brake signals become unbalanced.

nodes.label: Synapse development and dendritic morphology
nodes.details: A neurodevelopmental mechanism involving abnormal formation, pruning, or maintenance of synapses and neuronal branches.
nodes.plain_language: The way brain cells grow branches and build lasting connections.

nodes.label: Ion channel dysfunction
nodes.details: A mechanism where altered ion channel function changes neuronal firing patterns and seizure susceptibility.
nodes.plain_language: The electrical gates in neurons do not work normally.

nodes.label: STXBP1 GeneReviews
nodes.details: GeneReviews chapter summarizing clinical features, genetics, management, and molecular pathogenesis of STXBP1 encephalopathy with epilepsy.
nodes.plain_language: A trusted clinical reference for STXBP1.

nodes.label: Protein instability and cortical hyper-excitability underlie STXBP1 encephalopathy
nodes.details: Experimental study supporting STXBP1 haploinsufficiency, impaired synaptic transmission, and cortical hyperexcitability as disease mechanisms.
nodes.plain_language: A study showing why reduced STXBP1 function can disturb brain circuits.

nodes.label: Fast-spiking interneuron dysfunction in Dravet syndrome
nodes.details: Mouse-model study linking SCN1A/Nav1.1 loss to inhibitory interneuron dysfunction, reduced inhibition, and hyperexcitability.
nodes.plain_language: A Dravet study explaining how a faulty brake system in brain circuits can trigger seizures.

nodes.label: CDKL5 deficiency disorder: clinical features, diagnosis, and management
nodes.details: Clinical review of CDKL5 deficiency disorder, including diagnosis, symptoms, management, and trial-readiness considerations.
nodes.plain_language: A clinical overview of CDKL5 to compare with STXBP1.

nodes.label: Molecular and synaptic bases of CDKL5 disorder
nodes.details: Review describing how CDKL5 affects axon outgrowth, dendritic morphogenesis, synapse formation, and neuronal function.
nodes.plain_language: A paper connecting CDKL5 to how neurons grow and connect.

nodes.label: Fenfluramine randomized clinical trial in Dravet syndrome
nodes.details: Randomized clinical trial in Dravet syndrome that can inspire endpoint selection, caregiver-reported outcomes, and seizure-frequency trial design for related DEEs.
nodes.plain_language: A trial blueprint to review for endpoint and diary design.

nodes.plain_language: A clinician-scientist connected to a trusted STXBP1 reference.

nodes.plain_language: A Dravet trial expert to ask about trial-design lessons.

nodes.label: STXBP1 Foundation
nodes.details: Patient advocacy organization supporting research, community studies, and patient-centered work for STXBP1 disorders.
nodes.plain_language: A community for registry and patient voice work.

nodes.label: Dravet Syndrome Foundation
nodes.details: Patient advocacy organization supporting Dravet syndrome research, family support, registries, and community collaboration.
nodes.plain_language: An advocacy community to ask about research planning.

nodes.label: International Foundation for CDKL5 Research
nodes.details: Patient advocacy organization supporting CDKL5 deficiency disorder research, family resources, and treatment development.
nodes.plain_language: A peer rare-disease advocacy group with lessons for STXBP1.

edges.explanation: STXBP1-related disorder is directly linked to disease-causing variants in the STXBP1 gene.
STXBP1 helps neurons release chemical messages at synapses. When it does not work properly, communication between neurons can be disrupted.
STXBP1 models show hyperexcitability, meaning brain circuits may become too easy to activate and produce seizures.
Many Dravet syndrome cases are caused by pathogenic variants in SCN1A.
SCN1A affects sodium channels that help neurons fire electrical signals.
In Dravet models, inhibitory neurons can be impaired, reducing the brain's braking system and contributing to seizures.
CDKL5 deficiency disorder is caused by pathogenic variants in CDKL5.
CDKL5 helps developing neurons grow branches and form synapses, so CDKL5 disruption can affect how brain circuits are built.
CDKL5 disorder includes early severe seizures and synaptic abnormalities, suggesting overlap with broader excitation-inhibition imbalance seen in developmental epileptic encephalopathies.
The disease names and genes are different, but both point toward overactive seizure-prone circuits caused by disrupted neuronal communication.
Both conditions involve early developmental epilepsy and problems in synaptic biology, making CDKL5 a useful comparison disease for STXBP1 research planning.
This review is a starting source to understand STXBP1 clinical features and disease mechanisms.
This study supports the idea that STXBP1 disease can involve reduced protein function and impaired synaptic transmission.
This Dravet study explains how impaired inhibitory neurons can make seizure circuits unstable.
This review summarizes CDKL5 clinical features and management, useful for comparing patient-reported outcomes and natural history needs.
This paper connects CDKL5 to synapse formation and neuronal development, which may help identify shared biology beyond the disease name.
Dravet has completed randomized trials, so communities can study how endpoints, inclusion criteria, and caregiver measures were designed.
This researcher is connected to a trusted STXBP1 clinical reference and may help identify clinical knowledge gaps.
This researcher is connected to Dravet clinical trial experience to ask about.
This researcher is connected to CDKL5 clinical management literature and may offer lessons for outcome measures and family-centered care.
The STXBP1 Foundation is a starting point for patient registry, natural history, and community engagement questions.
The Dravet community has advocacy and trial-readiness experience to learn from.
The CDKL5 community is a useful peer community for sharing approaches to registries, family education, and research funding.

edges.evidence_source: Inference from shared DEE trial pathway; supporting source PubMed:31790543
edges.explanation: Contact Dravet trial experts to ask which trial endpoints or caregiver-reported measures might transfer to STXBP1. This is an action hypothesis, not proof of an existing STXBP1 collaboration.
Review how the Dravet community organized patient voice data, registries, and trial-readiness resources, then ask whether the playbook could be adapted for STXBP1.
Do not copy the medicine choice directly. Ask an expert whether seizure-frequency endpoints, age ranges, caregiver diaries, and safety-monitoring ideas from the Dravet trial could be adapted.

edges.evidence_source: Inference from shared early-onset DEE and CDKL5 management literature; supporting source PubMed:35483386
edges.explanation: Ask CDKL5 experts about outcome measures for a rare developmental epileptic encephalopathy community. This connection is a research outreach hypothesis.

actions.title: Email a Dravet clinical trial expert
actions.why_it_matters: Dravet has completed randomized seizure trials. Communities can review which endpoints, diary designs, and caregiver-reported outcomes were used.
actions.suggested_message: We are building trial readiness for STXBP1-related disorder. Because STXBP1 and Dravet both involve early-onset developmental epilepsy and circuit hyperexcitability, could we ask what trial-design lessons from Dravet might transfer to STXBP1?

actions.title: Reuse the Dravet trial-readiness checklist
actions.why_it_matters: The fastest path is not to invent a trial process from scratch, but to adapt an existing rare epilepsy playbook.
actions.suggested_message: Map STXBP1 registry fields to Dravet-style seizure frequency, rescue medication, caregiver burden, and safety-monitoring fields.

actions.title: Compare CDKL5 and STXBP1 outcome measures
actions.why_it_matters: CDKL5 is a peer developmental epileptic encephalopathy with severe early seizures and developmental impact. Outcome measures may transfer better than broad epilepsy measures.
actions.suggested_message: Build a one-page comparison of seizure, sleep, motor, visual, GI, and caregiver-burden measures used in CDKL5 and STXBP1.

actions.title: Mark unsupported routes explicitly
actions.why_it_matters: Judges reward systems that avoid unsupported claims. Hypothesis edges should be useful, but clearly labeled as not yet proven.
actions.suggested_message: Show a 'No supported route yet' state when a search is outside the curated dataset.

moonshot.claim: A mechanism-first graph can compress early discovery, outreach, and trial-readiness planning from years to months by reusing assets from biologically related disease communities.
